patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] mm/page_alloc: let the highest memory node recover from hopeless state

version_history.subject: [PATCH] mm/page_alloc: let the highest memory node recover from hopeless state

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a problem where the highest memory node in a system cannot recover from a 'hopeless' state, even when its zone recovers above the high watermark. The issue arises because the current code checks if there is another memory node available for allocations to fall back to by looking at the next higher-numbered node ID, which always returns false for the highest node. This patch changes the check to count the number of nodes with a state of N_MEMORY, effectively checking if any other node exists. As a result, the highest node can now recover from its hopeless state and kswapd will be re-enabled.

review_comments.author: Zi Yan
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Zi Yan questioned the dependency of clearing kswapd's hopeless state on a static memory topology, arguing that it should be reset regardless of available fallback nodes, as kswapd can go hopeless later if reclamation fails.
review_comments.raw_body:
Why does a runtime behavior, clearing kswapd hopeless state, depend on a
static memory topology (excluding memory hotadd/hotremove in this
context)? There is nothing telling us if a fallback node has available memory.

Just reset it regardless. kswapd can go hopeless later if the node
cannot be reclaimed.

BTW, LLM also points out that kswapd_try_clear_hopeless(), called by
direct reclaim, only clears hopeless when the node is balanced, but that
rarely happens. So hopeless state can stay much longer if there is only
one node. Adding Jiayuna, who added kswapd_try_clear_hopeless(), to gvie
some insight.

review_comments.author: Johannes Weiner
review_comments.summary:
reviewer questioned the premise of the commit, citing that it only added another re-wake event without removing any existing ones, and asked why this was considered at fault for kswapd getting stuck

Reviewer Johannes Weiner expressed confusion about the patch's logic, specifically questioning what 'having more than one node in the system' means for re-igniting kswapd on a single node, and suggested that the hopeless state code should be simpler, allowing kswapd to sleep until direct reclaim makes progress or other frees put the node back above high watermarks.
review_comments.raw_body:
This seems to be the express goal in the commit referenced by
Fixes:. Can you explain why this premise was wrong?

The patch in question also only added another re-wake event. It didn't
remove one. How can it be at fault for kswapd getting stuck?

---

I don't understand what "having more than one node in the system"
means for re-igniting kswapd on this one node.

Generally I don't understand what the heck we're trying to do with all
these patches against the hopeless state code. It shouldn't be that
hard, right?? If kswapd on a node failed for whatever reason, let it
sleep until direct reclaim makes forward progress, or other frees
(unmap, etc.) put the node back above the high watermarks (which means
enough of the unreclaimable pages were freed to justify a new wakeup
in the future to attempt reclaim against new pages).

Author acknowledged that next_memory_node() is not suitable for checking if another memory node exists, and will need to be revised in a future patch.

Author acknowledged that their previous patch did not fully address the issue and is submitting a new patch to complete its original intent.

tl;dr:  next_memory_node() is not the right check for what the

on a 2-socket system you would have:

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 0/5] mm: fix allocator races with memory hotplug

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/5] mm/page_alloc: detect zonelist rebuilds from memory hot-add
series_items.patch_summary: This patch detects and handles zonelist rebuilds caused by memory hot-add, which can lead to spurious allocation failures for __GFP_THISNODE callers. The issue arises when onlining a zone's first block rewrites the zonelists in place, causing concurrent allocations to fail. To fix this, the patch gates sequence checks on CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG instead of just CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE, ensuring that all configurations that rebuild zonelists after boot are covered.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/5] mm/page_alloc: validate zonelist slots against concurrent rebuilds
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a concurrency issue in the Linux kernel's page allocation system. When a zone is rebuilt online, its position in the zonelist can change, potentially leading to incorrect filtering and loading of zones by other CPUs. To fix this, the patch adds a validation check for each loaded zone against the highest_zoneidx and nodemask in both allocator loops. This ensures that only valid zones are used during allocation, preventing potential crashes or data corruption due to concurrent rebuilds.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/5] mm/page_alloc: snapshot the preferred zone against shrink rebuilds
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the `get_page_from_freelist` function to read the preferred zone only once, rather than at every use. This is done to prevent a kernel NULL pointer dereference that can occur when a concurrent zonelist rebuild replaces or nulls out the preferred slot. The change ensures that even if the preferred slot is replaced, a stale but valid zone will still be used, preventing the dereference error.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 4/5] mm/page_alloc: keep a zone's pagesets when it goes empty
series_items.patch_summary: This patch prevents the freeing of a zone's pagesets when it goes empty, which can lead to memory corruption and leaks. The pagesets are kept for the life of the zone, similar to pgdat->per_cpu_nodestats, and only folded in during zone_pcp_reset(). This change is necessary because setup_zone_pageset() now reuses existing pagesets and zone_pcp_init() keeps them when a node is re-added. The patch addresses an issue introduced by commit 340175b7d14d, which freed the pagesets when a zone became empty.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 5/5] mm/mmzone: read each zoneref slot once when filtering by nodemask
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves the performance of the __next_zones_zonelist() function by reading each zoneref slot only once when filtering by nodemask. The original code read the slot twice, which could lead to a NULL pointer dereference when offlining a zone's last block and rebuilding the zonelists in place. The patch fixes this issue by testing the zone directly after reading the slot, and it also removes unnecessary inline functions and simplifies the code.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses five races in the Linux kernel's memory allocator that can occur when memory hotplug is used to add or remove physical memory from a system. The issues arise due to concurrent access and updates of zone lists, page sets, and other data structures by multiple CPUs. The patches fix these problems by introducing retries for certain operations, ensuring proper synchronization, and preventing dereferences of NULL pointers. The approach taken involves modifying various kernel functions and data structures to handle the hotplug events correctly and safely.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3 0/7] selftests/mm: add MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT contract tests

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 1/7] selftests/mm: add MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT contract tests
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a selftest harness to test the behavior of MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT hints in Linux. The tests cover basic behavior, including that neither hint populates PTE holes or faults swapped pages back in, and neither can be applied to locked VMAs. Additionally, the tests pin the process to its starting CPU to ensure accurate results. This patch is part of a larger series of patches that aim to improve the testing of memory management features in Linux.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 2/7] selftests/mm: check MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT range handling
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds four new test cases to the selftests/mm/madv_cold_pageout.c file to verify the behavior of the madvise(2) system call when dealing with zero-length ranges, unaligned start addresses, and unmapped gaps in the range. The tests check that a zero-length range is accepted, an unaligned start address is rejected, and an unmapped gap in the range results in ENOMEM errors for both MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT hints. Only MADV_PAGEOUT has an observable effect on pages around the gap, so only its behavior is checked in this case.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 3/7] selftests/mm: check that MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT reject hugetlb
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a test to the Linux selftests suite to verify that the MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT hints are rejected when applied to hugetlb memory. The test checks that madvise(2) fails with EINVAL for a hugetlb VMA, as these hints cannot be applied to such memory. The patch also includes changes to reserve a hugetlb page for the test when run as root and restore the pool on exit.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 4/7] selftests/mm: check that MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT preserve shared memory
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a selftest to verify that the MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT hints preserve shared memory. The test checks three scenarios: a dirty shared file page is either written back or left resident, shared anonymous memory is paged out through shmem, and a SHM_LOCK'd segment remains unevictable without its VMA being VM_LOCKED. The patch introduces new functionality to the selftest framework, including a fixture setup and teardown for the test, and uses existing functions such as pageout_until_swapped to implement the test logic.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 5/7] selftests/mm: check MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT on partly advised THPs
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds self-tests to check the behavior of MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT on transparent huge pages (THPs). Specifically, it tests that paging out a whole PMD-mapped THP swaps it without corrupting its contents, and that pages outside the range stay mapped after paging out a base page or half of a PMD- or PTE-mapped THP. Additionally, it checks that MADV_COLD on half of either THP preserves its contents. The tests skip when PMD-sized THPs cannot be allocated, and the MADV_PAGEOUT tests also skip if MADV_PAGEOUT cannot swap.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 6/7] selftests/mm: check MADV_PAGEOUT file permissions
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a test to the Linux kernel's selftests/mm suite to verify that the MADV_PAGEOUT functionality works correctly when used by an owner of a file or someone who can open it for writing. The test checks that the owner can page out clean pages of their own files, and that unauthorized callers cannot unmap shared file pages or page out COW pages from private mappings. The test also verifies that MADV_PAGEOUT can swap out anonymous memory and unmap clean file pages in /tmp. If any of these conditions are not met, the test skips itself to avoid false failures.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 7/7] selftests/mm: check that unauthorized MADV_PAGEOUT skips large file folios
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a self-test to check that an unauthorized caller cannot page out large file folios when performing a partial MADV_PAGEOUT operation on a private mapping. The test creates a PMD-sized shmem file and maps it in two different ways, then checks that the pages of the file remain mapped even if the advised range only partly covers the file folio. This ensures that the system behaves correctly when dealing with large files and partial page-out operations.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series adds selftests to cover the contractual behaviors of MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT, which share a page-table walker in mm/madvise.c. The tests are designed to ensure that userspace can rely on these hints across changes to the walker's implementation. The patches add 24 tests that cover various scenarios, including faulting swapped pages back in, accepting locked VMAs, preserving shared memory, and paging out THPs. The tests also check whether MADV_PAGEOUT can swap/evict pages at all and skip relevant tests if it cannot. The patch series has been tested on a virtme-ng guest with 4 CPUs, two NUMA nodes, a 2G swap disk, and various configurations.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch addresses a potential performance issue in the cgroup/cpuset subsystem by introducing a retry mechanism when checking a policy nodemask against the current task's mems_allowed. The problem arises from the fact that cpuset updates rebind the task's mempolicy and change mems_allowed in separate steps, which can cause a spurious numa placement miss under certain conditions. The patch uses the mems_allowed_seq to retry the intersection until it is stable.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/2] cgroup/cpuset: use mems_allowed_seq when checking a policy nodemask
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Linux kernel's cgroup/cpuset code where a task's mempolicy could be rebound and its mems_allowed changed separately, causing a spurious numa placement miss when checking if a nodemask is valid. The fix involves retrying the intersection of the nodemask with the current task's mems_allowed until mems_allowed_seq is stable. This ensures that the check always sees the updated values, preventing a dropped nodemask and misallocated memory.

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary: Author disagreed that the patch's retry loop is intended to prevent dropping the nodemask on a race, explaining that it ensures stability of nodemask and mems_allowed when compared.
review_comments.raw_body:
No I don't think so. We're checking different things.

The loop here makes sure nodemask and mems_allowed are stable when
compared so we don't erroneously drop the nodemask on a race.

The cookie-check in check_retry_cpuset() determines whether the entire
allocation should restart.  It runs after the nodemask would already
have been dropped, so it can't catch this race.

~Gregory
